newsitem.title: COMOROS: Fresh clashes hit Comoros Anjouan island.
newsitem.headline: Fresh clashes hit Comoros Anjouan island.

text.p: Security forces on the Indian Ocean Comoros island of Anjouan clashed with pro-secessionist protesters for a second consecutive day on Wednesday, witnesses said.
France denounced the secessionists and said it respected the integrity of the archipelego.

"France respects the integrity of states and notably the integrity of the Federal Islamic Republic of the Comoros...and condemns separatist initiatives there," foreign ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said.

Clashes started around midday (0800 GMT) and sporadic gunfire was heard after angry youths set up roadblocks and burned tyres and security forces intervened in large numbers firing teargas. There were no reports of casualties.

"They (security forces) have dragged out two old ladies whose house is near the road and ordered them to remove the roadblocks," said one eyewitness contacted by telephone. She added that teargas was drifting into people's houses.

Authorities imposed a curfew on Anjouan's capital Mutsamudu on Tuesday after clashes in which many were reported wounded between security forces and youths protesting the arrest of pro-secessionist leader Foundi Abdallah Ibrahim.
Ibrahim, 75, was transferred with another pro-secessionist leader, Charikane Ahmed, to the main Grande Comore island on Tuesday.

Secessionists on Anjouan demanding independence from the Comoro Islands federation or a return to the French fold closed down the island's five prefectures on Monday in response to a government decision last week to outlaw two main pro-secessionist parties.

The Comoro Islands has a population of 190,000 and became independent from France in 1975. Residents of Anjouan, the second island, argue independence has brought only poverty, civil strife and numerous coups.
Rummelhardt said Paris also deplored the events of July 14, when three people were killed in clashes.

Three people including a gendarme were killed on Anjouan on Monday last week in clashes involving pro-secessionists who attempted to raise French flags on Bastille Day. Several people were killed in clashes in March.
